secb_sh:
#!/bin/bash

build() {
    echo "BUILDING THE PROJECT..."
    if /usr/local/bin/compile 1>/dev/null; then
        echo "BUILD COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "BUILD FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

repro() {
    echo "REPRODUCING THE ISSUE FOR flatbuffers.issue-9041..."
    /src/harness_bin /testcase/poc.bin
    # NOTE: YOU SHOULD NOT RETURN/EXIT 0 IN THIS FUNCTION.
}

patch() {
    echo "PATCHING THE PROJECT..."
    cd /src/flatbuffers
    if git apply /testcase/model_patch.diff; then
        echo "PATCH APPLIED SUCCESSFULLY!"
    else
        echo "PATCH APPLICATION FAILED!"
        exit 1
    fi
}

if [ "$#" -ge 1 ]; then
    command="$1"
    case "$command" in
        build) build "$@" ;;
        repro) repro "$@" ;;
        patch) patch "$@" ;;
        *) echo "Unknown command: $command"; echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
else
    echo "Usage: secb [build|repro|patch]"
    exit 1
fi
dockerfile:
FROM hwiwonlee/secb.base:latest
ENV FUZZING_LANGUAGE=c++
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y git
RUN git clone https://github.com/google/flatbuffers.git flatbuffers \
    && cd flatbuffers \
    && git checkout e223d69b36574c4a2b10dbd27761753de81624ab \
    && rm -rf .git \
    && git init \
    && git config user.email "secbench@local" \
    && git config user.name "secbench" \
    && git add -A && git commit -m "flatbuffers at e223d69b (pre-patch)"
WORKDIR $SRC/flatbuffers
COPY harness.cpp $SRC/harness.cpp
COPY build.sh $SRC/
RUN mkdir -p /testcase
COPY poc.bin /testcase/poc.bin

bug_report:
Heap Buffer Overflow in FlexBuffers ToString Post-Verification (google/flatbuffers#9041)

FlexBuffers VerifyBuffer validation is insufficient for the ToString accessor path. After verification passes, Reference::ToString calls strlen on buffer data that extends past the allocated boundary, causing heap buffer overflow during string length calculation.

A 20-byte malformed FlexBuffers input passes VerifyBuffer but triggers a heap-buffer-overflow (READ of size 5, 0 bytes after a 20-byte region) when ToString walks the decoded structure and encounters a string-typed element. The crash occurs in strlen called from std::string::append inside flexbuffers::Reference::ToString in flexbuffers.h.

The verifier validates buffer structure but fails to ensure string data boundaries are within allocated buffer limits. This affects JSON serializers, debug output systems, and any code calling ToString() after verification.

Severity: High (CWE-125: Out-of-bounds Read). CVSS 3.1: 7.5 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).
